newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Westpac says bad debt charges may rise.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Westpac says bad debt charges may rise.

text.p: Westpac Banking Corp said on Tuesday that the bank was close to the bottom of the debt cycle and that bad debt charges might start to rise again in future years.
"We'd be pretty close to it," Westpac managing director Bob Joss told a news conference, when asked whether Westpac's bad debts charges had reached a trough.
Westpac said earlier that its bad debts charge in the year to September 30, 1996 fell to A$121 million from A$330 million the previous year.
Westpac earlier reported that its net profit before abnormals rose 11.5 percent to A$1.132 billion from A$1.015 billion the previous year.
Analysts had on average expected a net profit before abnormals of A$1.12 billion.
However, the profit of A$1.132 billion included A$121 million of bad debt charges, down sharply from A$330 million in 1994/95.
Westpac shares closed 15 cents weaker at A$7.05.
